title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/self-interference-scan.ts, restore the reserved allowance on the state_depende
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/self-interference-scan.ts, restore the reserved allowance on the state_dependent_test_blame incident so the detector is not starved by the shared incident budget.

WHY. This change was landed once as fc7789c and then reverted by 734393a, a SECOND cutover of the same proposal that staged a snapshot older than HEAD. The surviving half declares "let blameEmitted = 0;" and sorts the offenders descending, but the condition on the push below it was reverted to the shared budget, so blameEmitted is now declared, never incremented and never read. It typechecks only because noUnusedLocals is not set. The detector therefore still competes for the same cap*3 budget as the rollback-streak loop above it, which emits 24 incidents; at the default max_incidents the detector reaches the array only when some other producer happens to leave slots free. Gap emission dedupes by incident kind, so a small reserved allowance is enough for the kind to always be visible.

THE CHANGE. Exactly one op, on an executable statement. Find this text, which occurs exactly once in the file:

      if (incidents.length < cap * 3) incidents.push({ kind: "state_dependent_test_blame"

Replace ONLY that leading condition so the line begins:

      if (blameEmitted++ < 5) incidents.push({ kind: "state_dependent_test_blame"

and leave the entire remainder of that line — every character of the id and detail arguments — exactly as it is.

WHAT THIS CHANGES AT RUNTIME. This is not cosmetic. It changes which branch executes: today the push is skipped whenever earlier producers have already filled cap*3 incidents, so the kind can emit nothing on a scheduled run; afterwards the first five offenders always push regardless of how many incidents precede them, and the sixth onward do not. It also makes the existing blameEmitted binding live rather than orphaned.

SCOPE. One replacement only, on that single line. Do not touch the "let blameEmitted = 0;" line, the sorted for-loop header above it, the "if (bset.size < 3) continue;" threshold, the detail text, or the rollback-streak loop. The allowance of 5 is deliberate: enough that the kind always files its gap, small enough that 55 offenders cannot flood a report other detectors also need room in.
